title: Coordinate ratios determine morphisms landing in one projective chart
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme, $W$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ any coordinate type, and $i\in I$. Suppose $f_1,f_2:W\to\mathbb P(I;S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] both have inverse image $W$ of the standard chart $D_+(T_i)$. If their composites to $S$ agree and they pull back every function $T_j/T_i$ to the same global function on $W$, then $f_1=f_2$.

source.place: Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), uniqueness paragraph, and the degree-one polynomial chart description

proof.text: Over affine S the i-th chart is affine. Its ring of functions is generated by the base functions and all coordinate ratios T_j/T_i. Equality on these generators gives equality of the induced ring maps (source closure_range_appLE_union_range_coordRatio).

The affine morphism correspondence identifies the restricted morphisms from equality of those ring maps. Since each inverse image of the chart is all of W, cancel the top-open isomorphism to identify the original morphisms. This is source hom_ext_of_preimage_standardOpen_eq_top.
